text:
li wei: Hey team  brand new X1 Carbon, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. I booted the corp image but during first-reboot LUKS didn't unlock automatically and system dropped me to a recovery shell asking for a passphrase I never set. FleetDM shows the device as "pending". Need to finish onboarding and get sudo to install my dev tools. Who can help with TPM/LUKS binding?

nina - IT: Welcome @li wei! Sounds like the TPM2 binding step (clevis/tpm2) didn't run during imaging. Don't try random passphrases. Pinging @amar - infra and @fleetdm-bot. Can you run `sudo cryptsetup status /dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-root` and `sudo lsblk -o NAME,MOUNTPOINT,FSTYPE,LABEL` from the recovery shell and paste output? Also what's the serial (`sudo dmidecode -s system-serial-number`)?

it-help-bot: Opening ticket INC-2026-22134 for Li. Please include serial and command outputs. Note: do not power off repeatedly.

li wei: Recovery output: `/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-root: not active`. lsblk: shows sda1 (EFI), sda2 (cryptroot), sda3 (LVM). Serial: SZ1234ABCDE. Attached pic: <recovery-prompt.png>.

amar - infra: Typical symptom when the imaging script that provisions the TPM2 sealing step failed. We can reprovision the key and rebind LUKS using clevis + tpm2-tools but that requires a short-lived local admin session while we run: `sudo apt install clevis clevis-luks tpm2-tools` then `sudo clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 tpm2 '{}'`. @nina can we grant a 90-minute temp admin?

nina - IT: Approved for 90m. Will DM temp account to Li. Reminder: session is audited and will auto-revoke.

fleetdm-bot: FleetDM note: device SZ1234ABCDE currently in state "pending". To complete device enrollment, run the Fleet enroll command provided in the onboarding email or `sudo fleetctl enroll --token <redacted>` once networking is up. If the device remains pending after LUKS is reprovisioned, reply here to request a manual enroll push.

li wei: Got the DM creds for temp-li. Logged in and installed clevis/tpm2-tools. Ran `sudo tpm2_getrandom 8` and it returned bytes. Ran `sudo cryptsetup luksOpen /dev/sda2 cryptroot` with the initial passphrase the imaging team left (from the onboarding doc) and that opened. Ran `sudo clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 tpm2 '{}'` and got back a JSON blob and OK.

amar - infra: Nice. Now run `sudo update-initramfs -u -k all` so the initramfs includes the clevis hooks, then reboot. Once it reboots the system should auto-unlock via TPM and you won't need the manual passphrase.

li wei: Rebooted. System came up to login screen and home mounted. FleetDM still "pending" though. What next?

fleetdm-bot: If the device can reach fleet.redwood.internal, run `sudo fleetctl get --host` to see host listing. If not visible, run the enroll command again. I'm pushing a remote enroll command now for serial SZ1234ABCDE.

fleetdm-bot: Remote enroll command pushed. Please accept the prompt if it appears.

li wei: Got the Fleet prompt, accepted. Fleet shows device as "online" and profile "developer-laptop" applied. File-based disk encryption (LUKS) shows sealed via TPM in Fleet attributes.

nina - IT: Great! Now that it's enrolled, I'll leave the temp-li session open for 60 more minutes so you can install Homebrew-equivalent (linuxbrew), docker, and add your SSH key. @dev-platform-bot note: new hire ssh key path question.

dev-platform-bot: For Linux laptops: generate an ed25519 key `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "li.wei@redwood.com"` and upload the public key to GitHub then submit via the onboarding form: https://redwood.company/secrets/ssh-upload (SSO required). If you need access to internal repos sooner, file an access request and include the public key.

li wei: Uploaded pubkey to GitHub and submitted via the form. Installed docker and my dotfiles. Encryption status in Fleet shows LUKS sealed and TPM bound.

vpn-admin: For VPN: we issue a machine cert after Fleet enrollment and Okta device sync. I pushed a provisional user cert to your Okta profile so you can connect immediately. Look for keychain entry labeled "Redwood VPN - provisional" or run `nmcli connection reload` and restart the VPN client.

li wei: Confirmed VPN connection works. One more Q: should I update to the latest Ubuntu HWE kernel now or wait?

amar - infra: Wait 24-48 hours to allow profiles and kernel module approvals to propagate; then you can run `sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade`. If you need a specific kernel for dev tools earlier, ask and we can approve it.

nina - IT: Closing INC-2026-22134 once you confirm Fleet shows "disk_encryption: sealed" and you no longer need temp access.

li wei: Fleet shows sealed and online; revoking temp access is fine. Thanks so much everyone, will post a short intro in #general later :wave:
